question: How do report egress and local semantic work vary while a fixed scope is surrounded by an adversarial label-heavy exterior?

productBoundary.playwrightRole: isolated Chromium harness and heap instrumentation only
productBoundary.baseline: opaque in-memory snapshot; never serialized by createSensor
productBoundary.report: descriptive; no expected result, task verdict, SVG, or pixels

protocol.exteriorComposition: 100% label[for] elements with missing targets; adversarial to historical document-global label lookup
protocol.scopeComposition: 54 fixed elements: section, heading, two buttons, status, list, 24 listitems and 24 spans
protocol.sameUnannouncedEffect: toggle aria-pressed and status text after mark()
protocol.candidateWireMetric: UTF-8 bytes of JSON.stringify(report); no network transmission performed
protocol.rendererCpuProxy: CDP Performance TaskDuration deltas around mark, action and read; mark/read exclude action and report serialization
protocol.actionMetricBoundary: action TaskDuration includes DOM mutation and scheduled mutation-radar delivery observable before the CDP response
protocol.heapMetric: noisy Runtime.getHeapUsage delta after forced GC; not a precise allocation measurement

interpretation: This tests the resident/scoped architecture, not browser automation or task correctness.
The opaque handle is two JSON bytes and contains no prior-state graph. The report is the candidate wire payload; this run performs no transmission.
Retained heap numbers are diagnostic and noisy; exact retained semantic node counts are the stronger local-state invariant.
The mutation radar covers the sensor root plus open shadow roots registered without gaps. NOT_DETECTED remains bounded to that stated coverage.
The exterior is deliberately label-heavy and adversarial, not a representative sample of all DOM compositions.
